item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it exposes the exact Upload signature, uses multipartbody.NewFile, preserves FilesOption compatibility, and covers the required failure and retry cases. It still duplicates Add and makes an out-of-scope RawClient change, so it would need tightening before merge.","reasons":["B implements the required signature exactly: Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption). A instead introduces FilesUploadOption, violating the specified API.","B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile directly. A adds NewFileWithFields and new multipart field machinery that the contract explicitly does not request.","B does not add association APIs. A adds seven association options and multipart fields despite the explicit prohibition on association fields.","B tests the multipart field, filename, payload, empty filename, nil content, source-reader errors, and retry behavior. A lacks a visible Upload source-reader-error test and devotes substantial coverage to forbidden association features."],"risks_a":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its request/response logic.","Changes FilesOption-related public APIs and excludes ordinary FilesOption values such as WithFilesQuery from Upload.","Refactors RawClient seekable-body and close-ownership semantics outside the requested scope, potentially affecting all reader-backed requests and redirects/retries."],"risks_b":["Upload also bypasses FilesService.Add, contrary to the requirement to centralize option handling, request construction, decoding, and errors there.","RawClient.Do now buffers every non-native reader unless WithNoRetry is set, a broad behavioral and memory-usage change explicitly outside the requested retry scope.","Buffering io.ReadCloser inputs can change transport-driven close behavior and leave ownership semantics unclear."]}
